results.name: Les Carmes
results.character: Medieval old town with narrow streets and a calm, historic atmosphere
results.what_to_do_there: Browse the covered Carmes market, admire Renaissance mansions (Hôtel du Vieux-Raisin), and discover the Miss Van "Songes" street-art fresco on rue du Pont de Tounis
results.why_it_is_special: Toulouse's essential old quarter — bordered by the Garonne and threaded by a Roman road, every street and square is packed with architectural wonders

results.name: Saint-Étienne
results.character: Chic, bourgeois centre-ville with imposing portals hiding private hôtels particuliers
results.what_to_do_there: Visit the striking Cathédrale Saint-Étienne, stroll Place Saint-Étienne, and wander narrow lanes that feel straight out of the Middle Ages
results.why_it_is_special: The quarter of the Renaissance merchants and the Capitouls (former city rulers); a photographer's dream of hidden courtyards and quiet elegance

results.name: Saint-Cyprien
results.character: Village-like left-bank neighbourhood with a cosmopolitan, bohemian vibe
results.what_to_do_there: Explore the Abattoirs modern-art museum, shop at the original covered market, walk along the Garonne riverbanks, and end with cocktails at a local bar
results.why_it_is_special: Toulouse's oldest cemetery (Rapas), the iconic Hôpital de la Grave dome, and a thriving food scene make it the city's hottest left-bank district

results.name: Arnaud-Bernard
results.character: Multicultural, lively quarter packed into just 4 hectares north of the centre
results.what_to_do_there: Visit the Basilique Saint-Sernin (UNESCO), browse the small-producers' market, and discover jasmine-lined pavements and a secret public garden
results.why_it_is_special: A historic gateway — once the Porte Royale where kings received the city's keys — with layers of Italian, Spanish and North African heritage and the tiny Théâtre du Fil à Plomb

results.name: Capitole / Saint-Georges
results.character: Grand civic heart of Toulouse, buzzing with café terraces and pink-brick elegance
results.what_to_do_there: Admire the Place du Capitole and its painted ceilings, visit the Jacobin Convent, and linger on the restaurant-lined Place Saint-Georges
results.why_it_is_special: The monumental square is the symbolic centre of the "Ville Rose"; the surrounding pedestrian streets lead to the Daurade basilica and the Pont Neuf with Garonne views
